current_activity: attacks the 5th Armored Division bridgehead at Wallendorf, hitting CCR on Hill 407 from the north
notes: Event date: 19 September 1944, early (MacDonald, ch. 3). Event definition: The brigade arrives on 18 September; on the 19th the LXXX Corps directs it to hit the main positions of Combat Command R of the 5th Armored Division on Hill 407 from the north, while infantry with Panzer Lehr remnants attack from the south; the Seventh Army has given it two thirds of its fuel; the Americans are ready (MacDonald, ch. 3). Event support: one source family (the US Army official history (CMH)). MacDonald, The Siegfried Line Campaign, ch. 3, p. 64: "directed the 108th Panzer Brigade to hit the main positions of CCR on Hill 407 from the north"; MacDonald, The Siegfried Line Campaign, ch. 3, p. 64: "the Seventh Army issued two thirds of its entire fuel supply to the 108th Panzer Brigade". Location: Wallendorf, Rheinland-Pfalz, the bridgehead village with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: Hill 407 lies in the bridgehead north-east of Wallendorf; the village stands for it, so the precision is 10 km and the confidence 0.5 (one family, approximate place). Location support: MacDonald gives the Wallendorf bridgehead and Hill 407. Opponents: US 5th Armored Division (Combat Command R).

current_activity: with the 404th Regiment, drives through Euchen and Birk and breaks into Bardenberg after dark
notes: Event date: night of 9 October 1944 (MacDonald, ch. 12). Event definition: With the 404th Regiment the brigade thrusts toward Bardenberg to stop the closing of the Aachen ring; after delays at Euchen and Birk, a force of about five tanks and 300 infantry overruns a roadblock after nightfall and pours into Bardenberg (MacDonald, ch. 12). Event support: one source family (the US Army official history (CMH)). MacDonald, The Siegfried Line Campaign, ch. 12, p. 297: "the 404th Regiment and the 108th Panzer Brigade had a hard time getting a thrust going on 9 October"; MacDonald, The Siegfried Line Campaign, ch. 12, p. 298: "The panzer brigade poured through into Bardenberg". Location: Bardenberg, Würselen, North Rhine-Westphalia (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: MacDonald names Bardenberg. Opponents: US 30th Infantry Division (119th and 120th Infantry). Relationship: attached to the 246th Volks Grenadier Division for the Bardenberg attack; the standing corps parent on these dates (the LXXX Corps relation of 19 September, or the I SS Panzer Corps from 12 October per Wikipedia) is not stated for this row in the sources read, so the validator warns that the attachment has no standing parent (Brigades Batch 3).

current_activity: remnants join the 116th Panzer Division attack toward Bardenberg and Euchen from Würselen
notes: Event date: 12 October 1944, early (MacDonald, ch. 12). Event definition: After the failure at Bardenberg, the Seventh Army reinforces the 60th Panzer Grenadier Regiment with Kampfgruppe Diefenthal, the remnants of the brigade and two assault gun units for an attack early on 12 October to push the XIX Corps back to a Bardenberg-Euchen line (MacDonald, ch. 12; Wikipedia: I SS Panzer Corps in October). Event support: two source families (the US Army official history (CMH), and Wikipedia). MacDonald, The Siegfried Line Campaign, ch. 12, p. 300: "remnants of the 108th Panzer Brigade, and two assault gun units possessing a total of thirty assault guns and howitzers"; Wikipedia, List of German brigades in World War II: "under I SS Panzer Corps ( 7th Army ) in October 1944". Location: Würselen, North Rhine-Westphalia (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: MacDonald names North Würselen and the Bardenberg-Euchen line. Opponents: US XIX Corps (30th Infantry Division).
